name: Combat Calligrapher
oracle_text:
Flying
Inklings can't attack you or planeswalkers you control.
Whenever a player attacks one of your opponents, that attacking player creates a tapped 2/1 white and black Inkling creature token with flying that's attacking that opponent.
blocked_sentences: Inklings can't attack you or planeswalkers you control.
Whenever a player attacks one of your opponents, that attacking player creates a tapped 2/1 white and black Inkling creature token with flying that's attacking that opponent.

needs.what: A permanent-duration attack prohibition that is scoped to a defending player AND filtered on the attacking creature's printed characteristics: an `affects` filter over attackers (here `{"subtypes": ["Inkling"], "controller": "any"}`) that forbids attacks against the source's controller and against the planeswalkers that player controls, asked at `combat.attack_target_forbidden` (which already takes a `planeswalker` argument) instead of `characteristics.attack_forbidden`. Needs a defender-scope flag so the planeswalker half is opted into rather than exempted.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `cant_attack` is the only static that filters attackers, and `characteristics.attack_forbidden` asks whether a creature may attack *at all* -- no defender is in the question. Using it here would stop Inklings attacking anybody, which is strictly stronger than the printed line and would shut off this card's own second ability (the tokens it hands opponents are meant to keep swinging at each other). The `cant_attack_player` op is the defender-scoped shape but is keyed only on the pair (attacking player, defending player) in `state.attack_restrictions`, carries no creature filter at all, and its `duration` (`this_turn`/`this_combat`) is required precisely because it is a resolving one-shot with no permanent to hang off -- so it cannot be a creature's continuous ability. `attack_tax` is defender-scoped and filtered but prices an attack rather than forbidding it. Finally, `combat.attack_target_forbidden` deliberately exempts planeswalkers from `attack_restrictions` (506.2, the Ghostly Prison reading), so even the op's mechanism has nowhere to say "or planeswalkers you control".

needs.what: `create_token` (and `copy_permanent`) should accept `attacking` as a player spec -- e.g. `{"binding": "defender"}` -- so a token can be put onto the battlefield attacking a named player rather than only the one the source itself is attacking.
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `attacking` is a bare boolean and `ops_board._attack_target` resolves it as `combat.attackers.get(ctx.source_oid)`, i.e. the player the *source* is attacking. Combat Calligrapher is never an attacker here -- its `creatures_attack_player` trigger fires off some other player's declaration -- so the lookup returns None and the token would arrive tapped but not attacking anyone, silently dropping "that's attacking that opponent" while still looking implemented. The `defender` event binding already carries exactly the right player (`triggers.EVENT_BINDING_KEYS`), and `primitives.create_token` already takes `attacking: int | None`; there is simply no key on the op to pass it through. The rest of the sentence is expressible today: `creatures_attack_player` with `controller: "any"` plus `defending: "opponent"` is "whenever a player attacks one of your opponents", `controller: {"binding": "event_player"}` is "that attacking player creates", `tapped: true` is "tapped", and the token id `inkling_2_1_wb_flying` exists.
